title: Four Shapes of the Same Care
logline: A mother's day moves between a toddler who needs feeding, a sick teenager who needs medicine, a young adult leaving for a first job, and a grown child on the phone from abroad who needs nothing from her at all.
human_question: Is it the same love wearing different shapes, or four different things that happen to share a name?

premise.story: An ordinary day, or a few days observed together, in a household where children are at very different life stages at once.
premise.place: A family home, the daily rhythm of a household spanning a wide range of ages.
premise.experience: Watching one person's attention change shape hour to hour without anyone ever naming what it is doing.

concept_links.why: The source's own image for the four sublime abidings is a mother with sons at different stages: wishing the infant well, wanting the sick child's pain gone, being glad at the young adult's good years, and stepping back from the one who needs nothing further [C095-P4:L39].
Compassion and sympathetic joy are responses that shift with who is actually in view, not a fixed mood [C024-P:L81; C024-P:L91].

what_camera_could_observe: Feeding and looking after the youngest child
Sitting with the sick child through discomfort
Quiet pride at an exam result, a first wage, or a departure for a new job
A phone call with the child furthest away, where she mostly listens
what_must_be_real: The family's actual daily life and real circumstances. Nothing staged or arranged to fit a four-part scheme; illness must not be treated as spectacle.

possible_arc.opening: Morning routine with the youngest child.
possible_arc.turn: A different kind of attention needed for the sick child.
possible_arc.ending_open: The phone call, or its absence, with the child who is furthest away.

requirements: A real family with children at genuinely different life stages, willing to be filmed over enough time
Full consent from every family member shown, including minors' guardians
No engineering of the household's circumstances to match the premise

suggestions.name: A fishing or farming household
suggestions.region: Trincomalee or Batticaloa district, east coast
suggestions.why: A region-level suggestion for geographic variety; no specific family or household is implied.
suggestions.verify: No specific family has been identified or confirmed.

risks: Staging illness or hardship for the camera
Casting a family to fit a scheme rather than following one where the pattern is already, even partially, present
drop_if: No family's real situation actually shows this range of care without being engineered for the film

connections.note: Both centre on sympathetic joy and its opposite, shown through real, unscripted human relationships.
Both ask how one person's care changes shape for different people within the same day.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
